newsitem.title: USA: USFreightways sees Q4 restructuring charge.
newsitem.headline: USFreightways sees Q4 restructuring charge.

text.p: USFreightways Corp said on Friday it expects to complete restructuring of its Red Star truck line in the fourth quarter and anticipates a charge against that quarter's earnings of about $0.10 a share to cover the costs of consolidation and realignment.
The final stages of the restructuring will require some terminal consolidation, the company said.
Improved operating results at Red Star, reported in the first and second quarters, continued in the third quarter, it said.
USFreightways today reported third quarter earnings increased to $0.49 a share from $0.40 in the year-ago quarter. Revenues rose to $343.2 million from $290 million.
Third quarter results benefited from a stronger economy, compared with the first and second quarters, and an improved pricing environment, it said.

As long as the level of economic activity continues at its present pace, and assuming there is no return to widespread price cutting, USFreightways said it will continue to improve its operating performance.

Operating income from all of the company's subsidiaries has been impacted by an increase in fuel prices. However, fuel surcharges have been implemented and will remain in effect until fuel prices return to more normal levels, it said. These surcharges, which will vary as the price of diesel fuel changes, should offset any future increases in fuel prices, it added.

Capital expenditures for the nine months ended September 28 totaled about $101 million, which included $27 million for the acquisition of a truckline. In the same period last year, capital expenditures totaled about $83 million.

USFreightways said its truckload subsidiary, Comet, continues to show satisfactory progress, increasing revenue during the current quarter. Although it recorded a small loss for the quarter, it is currently profitable, the company said.
USFreightways operates a group of regional, less than truckload, general commodities motor carriers in the U.S.
